title: docs(qa): 18.0 sweep anchor round 5 — the walled-posture and second-organization themes, runner environment facts, and two carried notes
body:
Refs #24579
Clause-②: no

Round 5 of the 18.0 release sweep's wave anchor (#24579), one PR in four parts. Rounds 1–4 landed as #24622, #24632, #24649 and #24671. This is a partial landing: the card keeps §2's other two themes and §4 for later rounds.

The diff is the checklist ledger and its runner docs only: four area files, `RUNNER.md` and `FOLLOW-UPS.md`. No product code, test or pin changes. Every edited area item takes one `revision` bump and one `history` row (ref: this PR). Every finding was re-derived from source before it was edited. The base is `bfc1539fe0`, merged with `origin/main` `92ce3af404` before this PR opened. Main's 8 new commits touched none of the cited sources except `.objectui-sha` (#24660 moved the pin `4016370a` → `12dc7b47c340`), and the one fact that reads it, the map-tile entry, was re-checked at the new pin. Findings that did not hold are left alone and listed at the end, each with the reading that refutes it.

## Part (a) — §2's two wave themes

**What the ledger allows.** `planned` is an item-level status only. `statusFieldProblems` in `scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs` judges `status` per item; a planned item must carry no `steps`; no clause carries a status of its own; and `checklist-select.mjs` drops a planned item from every runnable set. So a walled leg on an otherwise runnable item can only be recorded in `knownGaps`. The gate validates the `planned` shape and does not read `knownGaps` at all (PM H3).

**Where 18.0 refuses (PM H1 holds).** The walled refusal lives in one place: `walledPostureRefusal()` in `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`. `Serve.run` asks it right after the posture gate, before a config is read, a plugin is mounted or the HTTP server starts. `os dev` and `os start` boot through `serve`. The organizations-runtime load and `OS_ALLOW_DEGRADED_TENANCY` come later in the same method, so nothing skips the refusal. Kernel-level boots (`bootStack`, the dogfood wall suites) never pass through `serve`, which is why the pins still prove walled behaviour.

Measured live at `bfc1539fe0` with the built CLI:
- `os serve`, `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=isolated`: exit 1, `✖ FATAL: tenancy posture 'isolated' is not supported in 18.0 (NOT_IMPLEMENTED).`
- `group`: the same, naming `group`.
- `OS_MULTI_ORG_ENABLED=true`: the same, naming `isolated`.
- `single` (the control): passes the gate and stops later, on "Nothing to serve".
- `os start` under `isolated`: the same FATAL.

The refusal names no release ("an 18.x release"), so the knownGaps say "a later 18.x release".

**Where the second organization is refused (PM H2).** The door is `beforeCreateOrganization` in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts`. It answers 403 `ORGANIZATION_CREATION_DISABLED` wherever the effective posture enforces no wall, and on 18.0 that is every boot. Two more facts close the other routes: `sys_organization` declares `apiMethods: ['get', 'list', 'update']`, so the data API has no create, and 18.0 serves fresh installs only. Per-item decision: an org-switch clause is the §2 theme ("not scored on a stock 18.0 boot"). A planted second organization is a fixture route. QA run #24560 used one, a system write, and the knownGap says such a run must declare it. That route itself stays with §4.

**Shape.** The ledger has no area-level or README-level slot for a wave theme. An area file carries `$comment` and provisioning recipes, and a recipe must have a `provisioning.use` consumer. The README has no such section. `RUNNER.md`'s "Environment facts the runner should not re-derive" is the standing-facts slot runners read first. So each theme is stated once there, as the entries "18.0 boots the single tenancy posture only" and "A stock 18.0 boot holds exactly one organization". Each item's knownGap points at the entry and restates the refusal in one sentence with its anchor. That keeps the item readable on its own through `checklist-select.mjs`, and lets the anchor gate resolve each citation (a `RUNNER.md` anchor would red: the anchor floor file declares no floor for `RUNNER.md`). The entry also settles the verdict word. The live leg is recorded `skipped` with the entry cited, as the withdrawn ownership command's clauses are, and never `blocked(fixture)`. The sweep's records had scored it both `blocked(environment)` (QA runs #24557, #24559) and `blocked(fixture)` (QA run #24558).

**knownGaps vs planned, per item, on the four axes.** Every item below takes `knownGaps`. The common reason on each axis:
- *Business need.* Each item has runnable 18.0 clauses: its pin clause, plus single-posture clauses. The walled capability is built and pin-verified in-process. 18.0 refuses it at the CLI boot by ruling.
- *Long-term.* The clause stays where it is and returns when the refusal lifts. A planned split would duplicate clause text across two ids, delete the steps a planned item may not carry, and need a passing run to promote it back.
- *AI-error.* `planned` would tell the next sweep the capability is unbuilt, which is the wrong debt (README: "Scoring one as the other sends the next sweep to fix the wrong thing"). The knownGap names the exact clauses and the verdict word.
- *Startup scope.* No new ids and no new surface.

| item | fields edited | revision | run record | choice and why |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `platform-core.settings-organization-isolation-and-platform-rung` | `fixtures.knownGaps` (new, [0]); `acceptance[3].clause` | 1 → 2 | QA runs #24557, #24558 (c2, c3) | knownGaps. acceptance[0] (pins) and [1] run on single. acceptance[3] was a second walled leg: `settings-service.ts#organizationlessTenantKeyError` refuses only under a walled posture, and the pin asserts single does not refuse. So the clause is now marked `walled:` |
| `access-security.walled-environment-metadata-operator-only` | `fixtures.knownGaps` (new, [0]); `steps[0]` | 1 → 2 | QA runs #24556, #24558, #24559 (c1, c2, N0) | knownGaps. acceptance[0]'s pins are the 18.0 evidence. steps[0] now declares `sharingModel` (round 2's note): the admitted repeats in steps[2]/[3] reach the save door's authoring rules, which refuse an object with none 422 `security-owd-unset` (`validate-security-posture.ts#SECURITY_OWD_UNSET`, error tier). The walled refusal answers ahead of them (`meta-item-write-routes.ts`) |
| `access-security.activation-write-operator-gate` | `fixtures.knownGaps[0]`; `steps[8]`; `acceptance[4].clause`; `acceptance[4].verify`; `variants[1]`; `variants[2]` | 3 → 4 | #24579 §2 | knownGaps (re-grounded). The legs were `blocked(fixture)` on an "enterprise runtime" gap. On 18.0 the refusal runs ahead of the runtime load, and the runtime is open code since ADR-0132. Clause 5 keeps its unit pins as its oracle |
| `access-security.grant-table-write-contract` | `fixtures.knownGaps` (new, [0]) | 2 → 3 | QA run #24559 (c4, live leg) | knownGaps. Rounds 2–3 named acceptance[4]. ⚠️ The refusal's predicate is posture-independent (pin case "the predicate is the same on every posture"), so the leg is walled by its wording, not its mechanism. Recorded, not re-pointed: a single-posture rig is not measured here |
| `access-security.parent-and-organization-write-guards` | `fixtures.knownGaps` (new, [0]) | 1 → 2 | QA run #24559 (c1, live leg) | knownGaps. The emptied-organization refusal is a Layer 0 rule, and its pin's control keeps single unchanged |
| `access-security.no-active-org-session-semantics` | `fixtures.knownGaps[2]` (appended) | 2 → 3 | #24579 §0 / §2 | knownGaps. Every clause is walled, and the item is already `blocked {fixture, #9334}` with a pin. `planned` would also be wrong here: the capability is built and pinned. The marker is unchanged |

Taken, but not in the card's five: `no-active-org-session-semantics` (its clauses need a walled boot) and `chunked-upload-integrity` (the second-organization theme). Read and left alone: `platform-owner-email-anchor`, `suggested-binding-loop`, `public-form-withdrawal-layers` and the three attachments items carrying the CROSS-TENANT marker (see the end). No item in `automation.json` carries a walled or org-switch clause.

## Part (b) — `RUNNER.md`

`scripts/qa/` is not edited (ruling).

## Part (c) — `FOLLOW-UPS.md`

The file's own convention: append, never rewrite; a corrected row keeps its old content as "⚠️ This row used to …; DATE with #PR" (rows E2 and §6's second row), and a closed row carries its marker in bold (**FIXED in #N**, **closed by …**).

| §10b E3 | 615 | The stale tail ("… the other two are still owed") becomes "⚠️ This row used to end that …; **paid 2026-10-19 with #24649** (`cc95f5e63e`)". `rest-crud-config-contract` and `rest-batch-config-contract` (revision 3 each) name the mount pin in `automated.ref` and say in `knownGaps[1]` that the mount half is pinned. Measured in `api-backend.json` at `bfc1539fe0` |

"`showcase_approver_bindings` is draft on purpose" becomes `status: 'obsolete'` on purpose (`approver-bindings.flow.ts#ApproverBindingsFlow`). Its docblock says why not draft: a draft flow binds and fires like an active one. It is still the only flow on `showcase_field_zoo`, so the gap's conclusion holds.

## Findings left alone, each with its refuting reading

- **§6 "`scaffold-e2e.yml` has not run on the candidate sha; its latest scheduled run failed on `9112bcd8`"** (round 2). Re-read: still true. The newest `schedule` run is `9112bcd887`, failure, 2026-10-19T03:39Z, and only `pull_request` runs follow it. Not taken: it is a dated CI state that the next scheduled run changes, not a standing environment fact.
- **§6 "objectui live e2e is still red at its own pin `4016370a`"** (round 2). Not taken. It is §2's objectui-live-e2e theme, which the dispatch gives to the next round, and the pin it names has since moved (#24660 → `12dc7b47c340`). Not re-measured: that needs the objectui live suite.
- **`grant-table-write-contract` acceptance[4] "needs a walled boot"** (card §2, rounds 2–3). Half refuted: `grant-holder-membership-refusal.ts`'s predicate does not read the posture. The knownGap records this and keeps the clause as written. A single-posture rig, a grantee with no membership in the writer's organization, is a fixture route and is not measured here.
- **The card's "five items" list.** Not enough on its own: `no-active-org-session-semantics` (every clause walled) and `chunked-upload-integrity` (org switch) also carry the themes and were taken.
- **`platform-owner-email-anchor`.** No clause needs a walled boot: acceptance[5], the walled half, is test-only already. steps[0]'s parenthetical still reads "a walled posture … refuses to boot with it unset (plugin-auth init …)". On 18.0 the boot is refused earlier, set or unset. Noted, not edited: the item boots single and scores nothing on it.
- **`suggested-binding-loop` negative[1]** ("under a walled posture only the platform operator may accept"). A negative note, not a clause. Left alone.
- **`public-form-withdrawal-layers`.** Its `set-active` switches between the Default Organization and null, which a stock 18.0 boot can do, and it already puts the walled half out of scope.
- **attachments-storage `download-authz-both-sides`, `read-inherits-parent-rls`, `attach-requires-parent-edit` (the CROSS-TENANT marker).** That marker is about the dogfood matrix's `skipIf` block, already `blocked(dependency)`. None of their acceptance clauses needs a walled boot.
